Dacicus.definition: Dācicus ī, m a gold coin of Domitian, conqueror of the Dacians, Iu.

Dama.definition: Dāma ae, m a slave's name, H.

December.definition: December bris, bre, adj. decem, of the tenth : mensis, the tenth month (from March), December (of 31 days).—As subst m . (sc. mensis), C., L., H., O.—Poet.: Hic tertius, the third full year , H.; cf. me quater undenos…

Dialis.definition: Diālis e, adj. divus, for dīvālis, of Jupiter : flamen, the priest of Jove , L.: Flamen ad haec (sacra), O. —As subst: Dialis (sc. flamen), O.— Of the flamen Dialis : coniunx, O.

Diana.definition: Diāna or (older) Dīāna, ae, f for * Dī vāna, the goddess of light and of the moon (identified with *a)\rtemis): ad Dianae venire (sc. templum), T., C., V., H., O.: quem urguet iracunda Diana (i. e. an epileptic), H.— …

Dionysia.definition: Dionȳsia ōrum, n , *dionu/sia, the festival of Bacchus, the Bacchanalia, T.

Dis.definition: Dīs ītis, m DIV-, orig. deity ; hence, Jupiter of the infernal regions , C., V., O., Ta.—Of the Celtic god of night, Cs.: atri ianua Ditis, i. e. of the underworld , V.: domina Ditis, i. e. Proserpina, V.

Dryades.definition: Dryades um, f , *drua/des, wood-nymphs, dryads, V., O., Pr.

dactylus.definition: dactylus ī, m , da/ktulos (a finger), a dactyl.

daedalus.definition: daedalus adj. , dai/dalos, skilful, cunning: Circe, V.—Artfully contrived, skilful: tecta, V.

damma.definition: damma (not dāma), ae, f (poet. also m), DOM-, a deer, buck, doe, antelope, chamois (a general name for the deer tribe), V., H., O., Iu.— Venison : nil damma sapit, Iu.

damnatio.definition: damnātīō ōnis, f damno, condemnation, conviction : hanc damnationem duci non oportere: reorum acerbissimae: damnationem anteire veneno, Ta.: ambitūs: tantae pecuniae, to so large a fine : hae pecuniae tibi damnationi …

damnatorius.definition: damnātōrius adj. damno, damnatory, condemnatory : iudicium.

damno.definition: damnō āvī, ātus, āre damnum, to adjudge guilty, condemn, convict : reum: damnarent an absolverent: delicta mariti, i. e. believe him guilty , O.: causa damnata, decided unfavorably : contra edictum fecisse damnari: am…

damnosus.definition: damnōsus adj. with comp. and sup. damnum, injurious, destructive, pernicious : ingenia, L.: Venus, H.: libido, H.: artes, O.: bellum Romanis, L.: discordia damnosior rei p., L.: res damnosissima divitibus, L.: virtus …

damnum.definition: damnum ī, n 3 DA-, hurt, harm, damage, injury, loss : hoc lucri quantum ei damni adportet, T.: damna aleatoria: civitatum damna: amissi corporis, Ph.: cohortium, Cs.: post damnum sic, etc., after your ruin , H.: alien…

daps.definition: (daps) dapis, f 3 DA-, a solemn feast, sacrificial feast : adhibiti ad dapem, L.: obligatam redde Iovi dapem, H.: pro grege ferre dapem, for the protection of the flock , Tb.— A feast, banquet, meal, viands, victuals …

datio.definition: datiō ōnis, f 1 DA-, a giving : legum, the prerogative of legislation.—The right to convey, right of alienation , L.

dator.definition: dator ōris, m 1 DA-, a giver : laetitiae Bacchus, V.

dea.definition: dea ae (dat. and abl plur. deābus, C.), f deus, a goddess : di deaeque, T.: ab love ceterisque dis deabusque peto: bellica, Minerva , O.: venatrix, i. e. Diana , O.: siderea, i. e. Night , Pr.: triplices, i. e. the Fa…

dealbo.definition: de-albō —, ātus, āre de + albus, to whiten, whitewash, plaster : columnas.

deambulatio.definition: deambulātiō ōnis, f deambulo, a walking abroad, promenading , T.

deambulo.definition: de-ambulō —, ātum, āre, to walk abroad, take a walk, promenade. — Supin. acc: eamus deambulatum: Abi deambulatum, T.

deamo.definition: de-amō —, —, āre, to be in love with: te, I am greatly obliged to you, T.

debacchor.definition: dē-bacchor ātus, ārī, dep., to rave, revel wildly: satis, T.: quā parte debacchentur ignes, rage, H.

debellator.definition: dēbellātor ōris, m debello, a conqueror, subduer : ferarum, V.

debello.definition: dē-bellō āvī, ātus, āre, to fight out, fight completely, finish a war: cum Ferentanis uno secundo proelio, L.: debellari eo die cum Samnitibus potuisse, L.: proelioque uno debellatum est, L.: quasi debellato, as if th…

debeo.definition: dēbeo uī, itus, ēre for dehibeō; de + habeo, to withhold, keep back : alqd tibi absenti: tibi hoc video non posse deberi, i. e. you will not consent to remain my creditor.— To owe, be in debt : illis quibus debui, T.:…

debilis.definition: dēbilis e, adj. with comp. de + habilis, lame, disabled, crippled, infirm, debilitated, feeble, frail, weak : senex: membris omnibus: Ille umero, Iu.: equi, L.: Membra metu, T.: ferrum, V.—Fig., disabled, weak, helple…

debilitas.definition: dēbilitās ātis, f debilis, lameness, debility, infirmity, weakness, helplessness : linguae: pedum, Ta.: subita, L.: debilitate carere, Iu.: a se debilitates repellere, Fin .— Fig., weakness : animi.

debilitatio.definition: dēbilitātiō ōnis, f debilito, a laming, weakness : animi.

debilito.definition: dēbilitō āvi, ātus, āre debilis, to lame, cripple, maim, debilitate, unnerve, disable, weaken : debilitati inter saxa, L.: corpore debilitantur (saucii): vim ferro: opes adversariorum debilitatae, N.: Debilitaturum qu…

debitio.definition: dēbitiō ōnis, f debeo, an owing, indebtedness : pecuniae et gratiae: dotis.

debitor.definition: dēbitor ōris, m debeo, a debtor : creditorem debitoribus suis addicere: causā debitorum susceptā, Cs.: aeris, H.—Fig.: vitae tibi suae, indebted for , O.: manet officio tuo, i. e. bound to fulfil , O.

decanto.definition: dē-cantō āvī, ātus, āre, to sing off, keep singing: miserabiles elegos, H. — To repeat often, harp on, prattle of: mihi pervolgata praecepta: Nenia, H.—To have done with singing: iam decantaverant, i. e. were through …

decedo.definition: dē-cēdō cessī (inf. dēcēsse, T.), cessus, ere, to go away, depart, withdraw, retire: de alterā parte (agri), Cs.: de praesidio: ex Galliā Romam: e pastu decedere campis, V.: Africā, S.: praesidio, L.: naves suo cursu,…

decempeda.definition: decempeda ae, f decem + pes, a ten-foot pole, measuring-rod , C., H.

decempedator.definition: decempedātor ōris, m decempeda, a landmeasurer, land-surveyor .

decemplex.definition: decemplex icis, adj. decem + PARC-, tenfold : numerus hostium, N.

decemscalmus.definition: decem-scalmus adj., ten-thowled, having ten oars: actuariola.

decemviralis.definition: decemvirālis (xvirālis) e, adj. decemviri, decemviral, of the decemviri : leges, of the Twelve Tables , L.: annus: odium, L.: collegium.

decemviratus.definition: decemvirātus (xvirātus) ūs, m decemviri, the decemvirate, office of a decemvir : honor decemviratūs: perpetuus, L.—Plur., L.

decenter.definition: decenter adv. with comp. decens, becomingly, decently, properly, fitly : Singula quaeque locum teneant sortita decenter, H.: maesta, O.: pulsare decentius, H.

decentia.definition: decentia ae, f decens, comeliness, decency .

decerno.definition: dē-cernō crēvī (often decrēram, decrē rim, etc.), crētus, ere.—Officially, to decide, determine, pronounce a decision, judge, decree, resolve, vote : inter quos iam decreverat decretumque mutabat, alias, etc.: si caed…

decerpo.definition: dēcerpō psī, ptus, ere de + carpo, to pluck off, tear away, break off, pluck, crop, gather : pollice florem, O.: poma manu, O.: ficum, Iu.: Undique decerpta oliva, H.: fetū s arbore, V.: oscula rostro, snatch , Ct.—Fi…

decertatio.definition: dēcertātiō ōnis, f decerto, a decisive struggle : rerum omnium consulibus commissa.

decerto.definition: dē-certō āvī, ātus, āre. — In battle, to go through a contest, fight out: pari condicione belli secum, Cs.: proelio, fight a decisive battle, Cs.: proeliis cum acerrimis nationibus: vi contra vim: armis pro meā salute…

decessio.definition: dēcessiō ōnis, f decedo, a going away, departure : tua: tarda.— A withdrawal, retirement (from office): molesta.— A decrease, diminution, abatement : de summā: capitis.

decessor.definition: dēcessor ōris, m decedo, a retiring officer, predecessor , C., Ta.

decimus.definition: decimus or (older) decumus, adj. decem, the tenth (of a series): mensis, T.: hora diei: septuma (dies) post decumam, i. e. the seventeenth , V.: legio, Cs.: unda, O.: cum decumo efficit ager, i. e. tenfold.—The tenth …

decipio.definition: dēcipiō cēpī, ceptus, ere de + capio, to catch, ensnare, entrap, beguile, elude, deceive, cheat : eo deceptus, quod neque, etc., Cs.: etsi minime decere videtur decipi: Croesum: deceptus a me: per conloquium decepti, …

decisio.definition: dēcīsiō ōnis, f 2 decīdo, a decision, settlement, agreement : Roscii: nostra de aequitate: alcui decisione satisfacere.

declamatio.definition: dēclāmātiō ōnis, f declamo, practice in public speaking, oratorical exercise, declamation : in cottidianā: ut declamatio fias, a theme for declamatory exercises , Iu.— Loud talking, noisy talk : volgaris.

declamator.definition: dēclāmātor ōris, m declamo, a speaker for show, elocutionist, declaimer : de ludo: Vagellius, the ranter , Iu.

declamatorius.definition: dēclāmātōrius adj. declamator, declamatory, rhetorical : opus: studium, Ta.

declamito.definition: dēclāmitō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. declamo, to practise declamation, declaim : cum Pisone: causas, to plead for practice.—To talk violently, bluster : de aliquo.

declamo.definition: dē-clāmō āvī, ātus, āre, to practise public speaking, exercise in oratory, declaim: ad fluctum: Romae, H.: declamare doces? are you a rhetor? Iu.—To speak with violence, declaim, bluster: vehementissime contra me: ali…

declaratio.definition: dēclārātiō ōnis, f declaro, a making clear, disclosure, declaration : voluntatis a populo: amoris tui.

declaro.definition: dē-clārō āvī, ātus, āre, to disclose, make evident, reveal: praesentiam saepe divi suam declarant: ducis nave declaratā suis, N.—To announce, proclaim, declare (as chosen to office): hominis voce declaratus consul: ad…

declinatio.definition: dēclīnātiō ōnis, f declino, a bending aside, turning away, averting : tuas petitiones parvā declinatione effugi: atomi: corporis, Cu.—Fig., a turning away, avoiding, avoidance : a malis naturā declinamus; quae declina…

declino.definition: dēclīnō āvī, ātus, āre CLI-, to bend aside, turn away : ad dexteram de viā: si omnes atomi declinabunt (i. e. oblique ferentur): via ad mare declinans, L.— To deflect, turn away : agmen, L.: cursūs, O.— To avoid, evad…

declivis.definition: dēclīvis e (neut. plur. dēclīvia; once dēclīva, O.), adj. de + clivus, inclining downwards, sloping : in declivi loco, Cs.: vallis, Cs.: latitudo, i. e. a broad depression , S.: Olympi, O.: arvum Aesulae, H.: flumina,…

declivitas.definition: dēclīvitās ātis, f declivis, a slope, declivity , Cs.

decoctor.definition: dēcoctor ōris, m decoquo, a spendthrift, ruined man, bankrupt .

decoloratio.definition: dēcolōrātiō ōnis, f decoloro, a discoloring : ex aliquā contagione.

decoloro.definition: dē-colōrō āvī, —, āre, to discolor, stain: mare (caedes), H.

decoquo.definition: dē-coquō coxī, coctus, ere, to boil away, boil down, diminish by boiling: pars quarta (argenti) decocta erat, lost (in testing), L.: musti umorem, V.—To boil, cook: holus, H.: ardenti aeno, Iu.— Fig., to ruin oneself,…

decor.definition: decor ōris, m DEC-, comeliness, elegance, grace, beauty, charm, ornament : Mobilibusque decor naturis dandus, H.: signa decoris, V.: ovibus sua lana decori est, O.: imperii, Ta.: oris, Ta.— An ornament, decoration : i…

decoro.definition: decorō āvī, ātus, āre decus, to adorn, embellish, grace, beautify, decorate : te, H.: quem decoratum vidistis, arrayed in spoils , L.: oppidum ex pecuniā suā monumentis: dissignatorem lictoribus, surrounds , H.: nostr…

decorus.definition: decōrus adj. decor, becoming, fitting, seemly, proper, suitable, decorous : color deo: virginitati, L.: ad ornatum: decorus est senis sermo: silentium, H.: Dulce et decorum est pro patria mori, H.: decorum erat ipsis …

decrepitus.definition: dēcrepitus adj., very old, decrepit: Eunuchus, T.: anus, T.: decrepitā (aetate) mori.

decresco.definition: dē-crēscō crēvi, crētus, ere, to grow less, become fewer, decrease, diminish, wane, shrink: non mihi absenti decrevisse amicos: ostreae cum lunā pariter decrescunt: decrescentia flumina, H.: cornua decrescunt, disappe…

decumbo.definition: dēcumbō cubuī, —, ere CVB-, to lie down, recline : prior decumbas, take place (at table), T.: in triclinio, to fall, succumb, yield (of gladiators): honeste.

decuria.definition: decuria ae, f decem; cf. centuria, a division of ten, decuria, decade : hence, in gen., a division, company, class, decuria (of judges, summoned by the praetor to try causes): iudicum: senatoria: tertia equitum, Ta.

decuriatio.definition: decuriātiō ōnis, f 1 decurio, a dividing into decuriae : tribulium.

decurro.definition: dē-currō cucurrī or currī, cursus, ere, to run down, hasten down, run, hasten: rus, make an excursion: de tribunali, L.: summā ab arce, V.: iugis, V.: Monte decurrens amnis, H.: tuto mari, to sail, O.: pedibus siccis …

decus.definition: decus oris, n DEC-, grace, glory, honor, dignity, splendor, beauty : eius decus sustinere: verum decus in virtute positum est: regium, S.: muliebre, chastity , L.: casti pudoris, O.: sine decore perfugere, in dishonor…

decusso.definition: decussō āvī, ātus, āre decussis (decem + as), a coin stamped with X, to divide crosswise (in the form of an X), decussate .

decutio.definition: dēcūtiō cussī, cussus, ere de + quatio, to shake off, strike down, cast off : ense caput, O.: lilia, O.: summa papaverum capita baculo, L.: mella foliis, V.: silvis honorem (i. e. frondem), H.: turres fulminibus decus…

dedecoro.definition: dēdecorō āvī, ātus, āre dedecus, to disgrace, dishonor, bring to shame : familiam, T.: se flagitiis, S.: urbis auctoritatem: neque dedecorant tua de se iudicia, H.

dedecus.definition: dē-decus oris, n disgrace, dishonor, infamy, shame: sumptū s effusi cum dedecore: iudicia operta dedecore: domus plena dedecoris: vitam per dedecus amittere, dishonorably, S.: ob tantum dedecus amens, V.: nihil est de…

dedicatio.definition: dēdicātiō ōnis, f dedico, a consecration, dedication : sacerdotis: templi: aedis, L.

dedico.definition: dē-dicō āvī, ātus, āre, to dedicate, consecrate, set apart: templa Romae: aedem Castori: aedis Saturno dedicata, L.: simulacrum Iovis: Aridas frondes Hebro, cast, H.—Fig., to honor with a dedication: ut Fides, ut Mens…

dedisco.definition: dē-discō didicī, —, ere, to unlearn, forget: multa: haec verba: disciplinam populi R., Cs.: loqui: amare, O.: (amor) dediscitur usu, O.

dediticius.definition: dēditīcius ī, adj. deditus, surrendered : qui si dediticius est, S.—Plur m . as subst, prisoners of war, captives : vestri, L.: multitudo dediticiorum, Cs.

deditio.definition: dēditiō ōnis, f dedo, a giving up, surrender, capitulation : de deditione agere, Cs.: omnīs in deditionem accepit, Cs.: Cretensibus spem deditionis adimere: ad deditionem inpellere, S.: deditionis condicio, Cs.: in de…

dedo.definition: dē-dō didī, ditus, ere, to give away, give up, surrender, deliver, consign, yield, abandon, render: Ancillas, T.: te in pistrinum, T.: aliquem hostibus in cruciatum, Cs.: servum ad supplicium: neci, V.: mihi iuvencum …

dedoceo.definition: dē-doceō ēre, uī, ctus, to cause to unlearn, unteach, teach the opposite of: aliquem geometriam: (virtus) populum falsis Dedocet uti Vocibus, H.: cum a Zenone fortis esse didicisset, a dolore dedoctus est: ut coercend…

dedoleo.definition: de-doleō uī, ēre, to cease grieving, O.

deduco.definition: dē-dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere (imper. deduc, C.; deduce, T.), to lead away, draw out, turn aside, divert, bring out, remove, drive off, draw down: atomos de viā: eum contionari conantem de rostris, drag down, Cs.: aliquem…

deductio.definition: dēductiō ōnis, f deduco, a leading away, conducting off : rivorum a fonte: Albanae aquae. —Of colonists, a leading forth, establishing, colonizing : in istos agros: militum in oppida.—In law, an ejection, expulsion : …

deerro.definition: de-errō āvī, āre, to wander away, go astray, lose the way: in itinere: caper deerraverat, V.: sors deerrabat ad parum idoneos, fell upon improper persons, Ta.

defatigatio.definition: dēfatīgātiō or dēfetī gātiō ōnis, f defatigo, a wearying, tiring out, weariness, fatigue, exhaustion : membrorum: hostium, Cs.: defetigatione caedere desistere: miseriarum.

defatigo.definition: dē-fatīgō or dēfetīgō āvī, ātus, āre, to weary out, tire, fatigue, exhaust: se, T.: exercitum itineribus, Cs.: opus faciam ut defatiger, T.: diuturnitate belli defatigati, Cs.: iudices: numquam defatigabor ante, quam,…

defectio.definition: dēfectiō ōnis, f deficio, a failing, failure, want, lack, disappearance : virium: animi mei, despondency : solis et lunae, eclipse.—A defection, desertion, rebellion, revolt : facta datis obsidibus, Cs.: in defectione…

defector.definition: defector ōris, m deficio, a deserter, apostate : patris sui, Ta.

defendo.definition: dēfendō dī, sus, ere, to ward off, repel, avert, keep off : bellum, Cs.: ad defendendos ictūs, Cs.: solis ardores: frigus, H.: vim, Cs.: furorem, V.: crimen, to answer, L.: ignem a tectis, O.: solstitium pecori, V.: a…

defensio.definition: dēfēnsiō ōnis, f defendo, a defending, defence : urbis, Cs.: defensionis locum relinquere: defensionem in novo consilio parare, S.: criminis: contra crimen: causae suae: scripta: pro Cornelio, N.: ad istam orationem b…

defensito.definition: dēfēnsitō āvī, —, āre, freq. defenso, to defend often, practise defending : causas: sententiam.

defenso.definition: dēfēnsō āvī, ātus, āre, intens. defendo, to defend diligently, protect : alios ab hostibus, S.: umeros, O.: sua, Ta.: dum defensamus (sc. armentum), O.: defensantes, the guards , Ta.

defensor.definition: dēfēnsor ōris, m defendo, an averter, protector against : necis: calamitatum.— A defender, protector, advocate : quem defensorem paro, T.: tribuni defensores mei: illius, H.: culpae, apologist , Iu.: iuris: causae: op…

defero.definition: dē-ferō tulī, lātus, ferre, to bring away, carry off, take down, carry, take, remove: quae (dolia) amnis defert, V.: secundo Tiberi deferri, L.: ramalia arida tecto, O.: argentum ad eam, T.: litteras ad Caesarem, Cs.:…

defervesco.definition: dē-fervēscō fervī and ferbuī, —, ere, to cease raging, cool down, be allayed, be assuaged: dum defervescat ira: Sperabam iam defervisse adulescentiam, T.: cum cupiditates deferbuissent: quasi deferverat oratio.

defetiscor.definition: dē-fetīscor fessus, ī, dep., to become tired, grow weary, faint: Neque defetiscar experirier, T.

deficio.definition: dēficiō fēcī, fectus, ere (fut perf. defexit, old form. in L.—Pass., usu. deficior; dēfit, T., Enn. ap. C., V.; dēfierī, T.; dēfīet, L.) de + facio.— Intrans, to withdraw, revolt, desert, fall off : civitates quae def…

defigo.definition: dē-fīgō fīxī, fīxus, ere, to fasten, fix, set, drive, set up, plant: crucem ad civium supplicium defigi iubes: sudes sub aquā, Cs.: asseres in terrā defigebantur, Cs.: sicam in corpore: cultrum in corde, L.: telluri h…

defingo.definition: dē-fingō nxī, —, ere, to disfigure, deface, muddle: Rheni luteum caput, H.

definio.definition: dē-fīniō īvī, ītus, īre, to bound, set bounds to, limit, terminate, define: fundi extremam partem oleae ordine: orbem terrarum (loca): huius generis orationem, bring to an end. — Fig., to limit, define, explain: genus…

definitio.definition: dēfīnītiō ōnis, f definio, a limiting, defining, definition, explanation : hominum et temporum: iudiciorum.

definitivus.definition: dēfīnītīvus adj. definio, definitive, explanatory : constitutio: causa.

defio.definition: (dēfīō) dēfit, etc., rare passive for deficior.

deflagratio.definition: dēflagrātiō ōnis, f deflagro, a burning up, conflagration : futura caeli. — Fig.: deflagrationem Italiae minari, destruction .

deflagro.definition: dēflagrō āvī, ātus, āre, to burn down, be consumed by fire: incensa domus deflagravit: aedes, L.: Fana flammā deflagrata.—Fig., to perish, be destroyed: communi incendio: deflagrare omnia pati, L.: in cinere deflagrat…

deflecto.definition: dē-flectō flēxī, flexus, ere.— Trans, to bend aside, turn away, divert: tela, V.: amnīs in alium cursum: ad Romanos cursum, L.: novam viam, to build the road in another direction, L.—Fig., to turn away, lead astray: l…

defleo.definition: dē-fleō ēvī, ētus, ēre, to weep over, lament, deplore, bewail: meum discessum: haec satis diu defleta sunt: Numam, O.: membra defleta, i. e. the dead, V.: Haec ubi deflevit, uttered this lament, V.

defloresco.definition: dē-flōrēscō ruī, —, ere, to drop blossoms, fade, wither, decay, decline: flos tenui carptus ungui, Ct. —Fig.: deliciae deflorescunt: cum senectā res defloruere, L.

defluo.definition: dē-fluō fluxī, fluxus, ere, to flow down: (Rhenus) in plurīs defluit partīs, Cs.: Defluit saxis umor, H.: in Tiberim Orontes, Iu. — To glide down, slide, fall, descend: iam ipsae defluebant coronae: pedes vestis deflu…

defodio.definition: dē-fodiō fōdī, fossus, ere, to dig deep, dig up, make by digging: specus, V.: terram, H. — To bury, cover with earth: thesaurum defossum esse sub lecto: signum in terram, L.: novaculam in comitio: alqm humo, O.: iacen…

deformatio.definition: dēfōrmātiō ōnis, f 2 deformo, a deforming, disfiguring, defacing : tantae maiestatis, L.

deformis.definition: dē-fōrmis e, adj. with comp. de + forma, misshapen, deformed : deformem esse natum. — Formless, without shape : animae, O.— Unsightly, ugly, hideous, loathsome : qui senes ac deformes erant: iumenta, Cs.: agmen, L.: h…

deformitas.definition: dēfōrmitās ātis, f deformis, ugliness, deformity, hideousness : insignis ad deformitatem puer: in tantā deformitate, L. — Fig., baseness, vileness, turpitude : animi: fugae: ludicra, i. e. the disgrace of appearing on…

defraudo.definition: dē-fraudō or defrūdō ā vī, ātus, āre, to defraud, overreach, cheat: insuper (me), T.: Suom genium, i. e. by self-denial, T.: alquem ne andabatā quidem: ne brevitas defraudasse aurīs videatur.

defrico.definition: dē-fricō cuī, cātus, āre, to rub off, rub down, rub hard: dentem, O., Ct.—Fig.: sale multo Urbem, i. e. cause to smart, H.

defringo.definition: dēfringō frēgī, frāctus, ere de + frango, to break off, break to pieces : ex arbore plantas, V.: ramum arboris: ferrum summā ab hastā, V.

defugio.definition: dē-fugiō fūgī, —, ere, to run off, flee away, make an escape: ripa, quo sinistrum cornu defugit, L.: iniurias fortunae defugiendo relinquas, i. e. by death.—Fig., to flee from, shun, avoid, escape from: proelium, Cs.:…

defundo.definition: dēfundō fūdī, fūsus, ere, to pour down, pour out: odorem, V.: vinum, to decant, H.: pelvīs, to empty, Iu. — Esp., in libations: te prosequitur mero Defuso pateris, H.

defungor.definition: dē-fungor fūnctus, ī, to have done with, acquit oneself of, discharge, perform, finish: omni populari concitatione: periculis: honoribus: proelio, L.: unius poenā, L.: laboribus, H.: defuncta corpora vitā, dead, V.: t…

degener.definition: dē-gener is, adj. de + genus, inferior to ancestors, degenerate : Neoptolemum, V.: hi iam degeneres sunt, mixti, L.: dignitate formae, Ta.— Unworthy : patrii non degener oris, i. e. inheriting a father's eloquence , O…

degenero.definition: dēgenerō āvī, ātus, āre degener, to be inferior to ancestors, decline, be degenerate : a vobis: Pandione nata, degeneras! O.: Macedones in Syros degenerarunt, L.—Fig., to fall off, decline, degenerate : ut consuetudo …

dego.definition: dēgō dēgī, —, ere de + ago, of time, to spend, pass : cum uno aetatem, T.: inter feras aetatem: expertem sine crimine vitam, V.: otia in thalamo, Ct.: vita, quae cum virtute degatur: aetatis degendae ratio: laetus deg…

degrandinat.definition: dē-grandinat impers, it stops hailing, O.

degravo.definition: dē - gravō —, ātus, āre, to weigh down, overpower, burden: caput, O.: circumventum cornu, L.: onere degravati, Ph. — Fig., to drag down, burden, incommode: peritos nandi volnera degravant, L.: gremium, O.

degredior.definition: dēgredior gressus, ī, dep. de + gradior, to go down, march down, descend : paulum ex eo loco, Cs.: ex arce, L.: monte, S.: in aequum, Ta.: ad pedes, to alight, dismount , L.

degrunnio.definition: dē - grunniō —, —, īre, to grunt out, do his grunting, Ph.

degusto.definition: dē-gustō āvī, ātus, āre, to taste: inde (sc. de sanguine), S.—Poet.: (lancea) summum degustat volnere corpus, i. e. grazes, V. — Fig., to get as a sample, taste, try, make trial of, test: genus hoc exercitationum: ex …

dehinc.definition: de-hinc (monosyi., V., O.), adv., from this time, henceforth, hereafter, for the future: nunc dehinc spero aeternam inter nos gratiam Fore, T.: ne exspectetis argumentum, for the rest, T.: Tarquinium quācunque dehinc …

dehisco.definition: de-hīscō —, —, ere, to part, divide, split open, gape, yawn: vel tellus mihi dehiscat, V.: terrae dehiscunt, V.: rimis dehiscit cumba, O.: dehiscens intervallis hostium acies, L.

dehonestamentum.definition: dehonestāmentum ī, n dehonesto, that which disfigures, a blemish, disgrace, dishonor : oris, Ta.: nullum insigne, Ta.

dehonesto.definition: de-honestō —, —, āre, to disgrace, dishonor: famam, L.: proavum infami operā, Ta.

dehortor.definition: de-hortor ātus, ārī, dep., to advise to the contrary, dissuade: me: me a vobis, from your cause, S.: me ne darem, T.: plura scribere me, S.

deicio.definition: dēiciō or dēiiciō iēcī, iectus, ere de + iacio, to throw down, hurl down, precipitate, prostrate, raze, fell, cut down, tear down, destroy : alqm de ponte in Tiberim: alqm de saxo (Tarpeio), L.: a cervicibus iugum: se…

deinceps.definition: deinceps (disyl., H.), adv. dein + CAP-.—In space, one after another, in order, in succession : cum deinceps ex primis versuum litteris aliquid conectitur: prima Curene est, ac deinceps duae Syrtes, S.: tres deinceps …

deinde.definition: deinde (in poetry two syll.), or dein (in poetry one syll.), adv. de + locat. suffix -im + demonstr. -de.—In space, then, next, thereafter, thence : via interest perangusta, deinde paulo latior patescit campus, L.: du…

delabor.definition: dē-lābor lapsus, ī, dep., to fall, sink, slip down, glide down, descend: in mare (flumen), H.: medios delapsus in hostīs, V.: gradibus, by the steps, O.: signum de caelo delapsum: de manibus civium delapsa arma: ex eq…

delamentor.definition: dē-lāmentor —, ārī, dep., to lament, bewail: natam ademptam, O.

delasso.definition: dē-lassō —, —, āre, to wear out, tire: Fabium, H.

delatio.definition: dēlātiō ōnis, f de + TAL-, an accusation, denunciation : nominis, an indictment : ne haec mihi delatio detur: socius delationis, Ta.

delator.definition: dēlātor ōris, m de + TAL-, an informer, denouncer : criminum, L.: amici, Iu.: cum plena litora multo Delatore forent, Iu.: maiestatis, of high-treason , Ta.

delectabilis.definition: dēlectābilis e, adj. delecto, delightful, agreeable : cibus, Ta.

delectamentum.definition: dēlectāmentum ī, n delecto, a delight, amusement, sport : sibi me pro delectamento putat, T.: delectamenta puerorum.

delectatio.definition: dēlectātiō ōnis, f delecto, a delighting, delight, pleasure, amusement, satisfaction : nulla alia, T.: oculorum: ridendi: conviviorum: mira in cognoscendo: suae delectationis causā .

delecto.definition: dēlectō āvī, ātus, āre, intens. de + lacio, to allure, attract, delight, charm, please, entertain, interest : haec studia delectant domi volunt delectare poetae, H.: me: delectari multis rebus: imperio, Cs.: criminibu…

delegatio.definition: dēlēgātiō ōnis, f delego, an assignment (of debt), substitution : a mancipe.

delenimentum.definition: dēlēnīmentum ī, n delenio, a blandishment, allurement : animis obicere, L.: delenimenta vitiorum, i. e. effeminate luxuries , Ta.

delenio.definition: dē-lēniō īvī, ītus, īre, to soothe, soften, charm, captivate, entice, cajole, fascinate: se donis: milites blande appellando: Midan carmine, O.: instrumento voluptatum militum animos, L.: dolentem, H.: dolorem remedii…

delenitor.definition: dēlēnītor ōris, m delenio, a soother, charmer : cuius (iudicis) orator.

deleo.definition: dēleō ēvī (dēlērat, C.; dē lēsset, L.), ētus, ēre de + LI-, to erase, efface, obliterate, blot out : epistulas: cum tabulas prehendisset, digito legata delevit: Non delenda carmina, H.: tabellas, O.: tabulas, Iu.— In …

deletrix.definition: dēlētrīx īcis, f delco, a destroyer : imperi.

deliberabundus.definition: dēlīberābundus adj. delibero, pondering, reflecting : velut deliberabundus, in a brown study , L.

deliberatio.definition: dēlīberātiō ōnis, f delibero, a deliberation, consultation, consideration : de re p.: haec deliberatio, quemnam, etc.: habet res deliberationem, needs consideration : consili capiendi, upon the measure to be adopted :…

deliberativus.definition: dēlīberātīvus adj. delibero, deliberative : genus (rerum), subjects requiring deliberation : causa.

deliberator.definition: dēlīberātor ōris, m delibero, one who ponders, a delayer : ille, that man of hesitation .

deliberatus.definition: dēlīberātus adj. with comp. P. of delibero, resolved upon, determined : Deliberatā morte ferocior, H.: neque illi quicquam deliberatius fuit quam, etc.

delibero.definition: dē-līberō āvī, ātum, āre de + libra, to weigh well, consider maturely, deliberate, ponder, meditate, take counsel, consult, advise upon : re deliberatā, Cs.: hoc, T.: de summā rerum, Cs.: de bello: quid intersit suā: …

delibo.definition: dē-lībō āvī, ātus, āre, to take, enjoy, pluck, gather: flos delibatus populi, the picked flower: omnīs undique flosculos, cull: novum honorem, L.: oscula, V.: artīs, O.—To take away, detract, subtract, remove: de laud…

delibro.definition: dē-librō —, ātus, āre de + 4 liber, to take off the rind, bark, peel : (arborum) delibratis cacuminibus, Cs.

delicatus.definition: dēlicātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of * dēlicō, to clear up, alluring, charming, pleasing, delightful, luxurious, voluptuous : in illo delicatissimo litore: hortuli, Ph.: puerorum comitatus: delicatiores in cantu f…

deliciolae.definition: dēliciolae ārum, f dim. deliciae, a darling : nostrae, Tulliola.

delicium.definition: dēlicium ī, n de + 1 LAC-, a sweetheart , Ph.

delinquo.definition: dē-linquō līquī, lictus, ere, to fail, be wanting, fall short, trespass, err, commit a fault, do wrong, transgress, offend: quod populi adversus P. R. deliquerunt, L. (old formula): ut condemnaretur filius si pater de…

deliquesco.definition: de-liquēscō licuī, —, ere, to melt away, dissolve, melt: Hyrie flendo delicuit, O.—Fig.: qui nec alacritate futtili gestiens deliquescat.

deliratio.definition: dēlīrātiō ōnis, f deliro, giddiness, silliness, folly, dotage, madness : incredibilis.

deliro.definition: dēlīrō —, —, āre delirus, to be crazy, be deranged, be silly, dote, rave : decipi tam dedecet quam delirare: timore, T.: in extis totam Etruriam delirare: Stertinium deliret acumen, H.: quicquid delirant reges, whatev…

delirus.definition: dēlīrus adj. de + lira, silly, doting, crazy : senex: anus: mater, H.

delitigo.definition: dē-lītigō —, —, āre, to scold, rail: tumido ore, H.

delubrum.definition: dēlūbrum ī, n de + 3 LV-, a place of cleansing, temple, shrine, sanctuary : audita ex delubro vox, L.: delubrum eius in oppido dedicaverunt: ex alto delubri culmine, V.: deorum delubra.

deludo.definition: dē-lūdō sī, sus, ere, to play false, mock, deceive, make sport of, delude: in hac re me deludier, T.: deludi vosmet a tribuno patiemini?: dolis me, T.: animum responso, V.: quā (linguā) sum delusa, O.: quae sopitos de…

delumbo.definition: dēlumbō —, —, āre de + lumbus, to enervate, weaken : sententias.

demadesco.definition: de-madēscō maduī, —, ere, to become wet, be moistened, O.

demando.definition: dē-mandō āvī, ātus, āre, to give in charge, intrust, commit: pueri unius curae demandabantur, L.: curam (sauciorum) legatis, L.

demano.definition: dē-mānō —, —, āre, to flow down, glide down, Ct.

demens.definition: dē-mēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup, out of one's senses, insane, demented, mad, raving, foolish, distracted: Adeon est demens? T.: num quis est igitur tam demens, qui, etc.: quid est enim dementius, quam, etc.?: A…

dementia.definition: dēmentia ae, f demens, insanity, madness, distraction, folly : ut est Dementia, so mad is he , T.: O hanc dementiam, T.: exspectare ... summae dementiae esse iudicabat, Cs.: per dementiam cuncta agere, S.: quae te dem…

demereo.definition: dē-mereō uī, —, ēre, to deserve well of: Crimine te meo, O.

demergo.definition: dē-mergō sī, sus, ere, to sink, submerge, plunge, dip, immerse, bury: caput: demersis rostris, V.: in Tusci demersus fluminis undis, O.: naves, L.: orbes (of the sun), i. e. to set, O.: dapes in alvum, O. — Fig., to p…

demetior.definition: (dē-mētior) mēnsus, īrī, dep., to measure off, measure out.—Only P. perf.: verba verbis quasi demensa.

demeto.definition: dē-metō messuī, messus, ere, to mow, reap, cut off, gather, crop, harvest: tempora demetendis fructibus accommodata: demesso frumento, Cs.: alienos agros: pollice florem, to pluck, V.: huic ense caput, to behead, O.

demigratio.definition: dēmigrātiō ōnis, f demigro, an emigration , N.

demigro.definition: dē-migrō āvī, ātus, āre, to migrate, emigrate, move, depart, remove, go away: ex his aedificiis, Cs.: in urbem ex agris, L.: in alias terras: ad Marcellum: aliquo: hinc, i. e. to die: demigrandi causā, Cs.: ex hominum…

deminuo.definition: dē-minuō uī, ūtus, ere, to make smaller, lessen, diminish: deminutae copiae, Cs.: militum vires inopia frumenti deminuerat, Cs.: de bonis, i. e. to alienate in part: praedia. — Fig., to take away, abate, lessen, reduc…

deminutio.definition: dēminūtiō (dīm-) ōnis, f deminuo, a diminution, decrease, lessening, abatement : luminis: civium: vectigalium: de bonis privatorum: provinciae, of the term of office .—In law: datio deminutio, the right of alienation,…

demiror.definition: dē-mīror —, ārī, dep., to wonder, be amazed: (haec vos) sperasse me consule adsequi posse demiror: hoc, qui potueris, etc., I cannot imagine, T.: Quid sit, etc., T.: cur, etc.

demissio.definition: dēmissiō ōnis, f demitto, a letting down, sinking, lowering : storiarum, Cs.—Fig., dejection : animi.

demissus.definition: dēmissus adj. with comp. P. of demitto.— Of places, lowered, sunken, low-lying, low : loca, Cs. — Drooping, falling, hanging down, low : Demissis umeris esse, T.: labia, T.: si demissior ibis, fly too low , O.: demiss…

demitigo.definition: dē-mītigō —, —, āre, to make mild: cottidie demitigamur, grow more lenient.

demitto.definition: de-mittō mīsī, missus, ere, to send down, let down, drop, lower, put down, let fall, sink: lacrimas, shed, V.: ubera, let down, V.: ancilia caelo demissa, L.: latum clavum pectore, H.: Maiā genitum demittit ab alto, V…

demo.definition: dēmō dēmpsī, dēmptus, ere de+emo, to take away, take off, subtract, remove, withdraw : haec (epistula) ad turrim adhaesit ... dempta ad Ciceronem defertur, Cs.: semper alqd demendo: Caudae unum (pilum), H.: aurum sibi…

demolitio.definition: dēmōlītiō ōnis, f demolior, a tearing down, demolishing : ea (statuarum): signorum.

demonstratio.definition: dēmōnstrātiō ōnis, f demonstro, a showing, pointing out, description : gestus sententiam demonstratione declarans: conversam habere.— An exposition, explanation : huius generis: quem ad modum quidque fiat.— Demonstrat…

demonstrativus.definition: dēmōnstrātīvus adj. demonstro, designating, demonstrative : genus (orationis), a branch of rhetoric employed in depicting a person .

demonstrator.definition: dēmōnstrātor ōris, m demonstro, one who points out, an indicator, guide : unius cuiusque sepeliendi.

demonstro.definition: dē-mōnstrō āvī, ātus, āre, to point out, indicate, designate, show: figuram digito: ubi habitet (mihi) demonstrarier, T.: itinera: quid ubique esset: finīs, i. e. to deliver possession (of land): demonstrant astra sal…

demorior.definition: (dē-morior) mortuus, ī, to die off, die (out of a number): sacerdotes demortui sunt novique suffecti, L.: ex veterum numero senator: emere in demortui locum: in demortui locum censor sufficitur, L.

demoror.definition: dē-moror ātus, ārī, dep., to retard, detain, delay: vos: hoste iter demorante, Cs.: Teucros armis, restrain from battle, V.: fando Austros, V.: annos, i. e. remain alive, V.: mortalia arma, i. e. await, V.: nihil demo…

demoveo.definition: dē-moveō mōvī, mōtus, ēre, to move away, put away, remove, expel, drive out: demoveri de loco: ex possessione rem p.: hostes gradu demoti, driven back, L.: vestri facti praeiudicio demotus, forced to yield, Cs.—Fig., …

demugitus.definition: dēmūgītus adj. de + mugio, bellowing, resounding with herds : paludes, O.

demulceo.definition: dē-mulceō —, —, ēre, to stroke down, stroke caressingly: tibi caput, T.: dorsum, L.

demurmuro.definition: dē-murmurō —, —, āre, to mutter over: carmen, O.

demutatio.definition: dēmūtātīō ōnis, f demuto, a degeneracy, perversion : morum.

demuto.definition: dē-mūtō āvī, ātus, āre, to change, alter: placitum ‘instituto flaminum nihil demutari,’ Ta.

denarius.definition: dēnārius (gen plur. -iūm; rarely -iōrum), adj. deni, containing ten each ; hence, worth ten (asses): nummus, a silver coin, originally of ten, afterwards of sixteen asses (about 8 d ., $0.16): pendere denarios nummos …

denarro.definition: dē-nārrō —, —, āre, to tell, relate, narrate: Haec illi, T.: matri, ut, etc., H.

denato.definition: dē-natō —, —, āre, to swim down: Tusco alveo, H.

denego.definition: dē-negō āvī, ātus, āre, to reject, refuse, deny: denegandi pudor, T.: conloquia denegata, Cs.: mihi, to say no: quod antea petenti denegasset, Cs.: quod iracundiae denegavisti: honorem homini: operam rei p.: se commis…

deni.definition: dēnī ae, a (gen. dēnūm, C.; dē nōrum, L.), num distrib., ten each, ten at a time, by tens: uxo res habent deni inter se communīs, Cs.: uxores denas habere, S.: pueri annorum septenūm denūm.—Ten (poet. for decem): Bis …

denicalis.definition: dēnicālis e, adj. de + nex, purifying from death : feriae, a service for purification, after a death in the household .

denique.definition: dēnique adv., and thenceforward, and thereafter, at last, at length, finally, lastly, only, not until : denique Metuebant me, T.: Metui, quid futurum denique esset, T.: post biennium denique appellas: octavo denique m…

denomino.definition: dē-nōminō āvī, ātus, āre, to call, name: (ab Lamo) Lamiae denominati, H.

denormo.definition: dē-nōrmō —, —, āre de + norma, to disfigure, make irregular : (angulus) agellum, H.

denoto.definition: dē-notō āvī, ātus, āre, to mark out, point out, specify, indicate, designate: civīs Romanos trucidandos: Icilios denotante senatu, L.—Fig., to take note of, mark, observe closely: denotandis hominum palloribus, Ta.: r…

dens.definition: dēns dentis, m ED-, a tooth : dentibus in ore constructis: eorum adversi acuti ... intimi, qui genuini vocantur, the front teeth ... grinders : puer, nondum omni dente renato, Iu.: dentī s exacuit sus, tusks , V.: vip…

densus.definition: dēnsus adj. with comp. and sup, thick, close, compact, dense, crowded: silva: densiores silvae, Cs.: densissimae silvae, Cs.: densum umeris volgus, H.: litus, sandy, O.: caligo, V.: densissima nox, pitch-dark, O.: pin…

dentalia.definition: dentālia ium, n dens, the share-beam (of a plough), V.

dentatus.definition: dentātus adj. dens, having teeth : serrula: male, O.— Polished with a tooth : charta.

denubo.definition: dē-nūbō ūpsī, ūptus, ere, to marry away, go away in marriage: in ullos thalamos, O.—To marry beneath one's rank: in domum Blandi.— Cf a mock marriage: in modum solemnium confugiorum, Ta.

denudo.definition: dē-nūdō āvī, ātus, āre, to lay bare, make naked, denude, uncover: denudatis ossibus: ne denudeter a pectore.— Fig., to disclose, reveal, detect, betray, expose: indicia sua, L.: mihi suum consilium, L. —To strip, plun…

denuntiatio.definition: dēnūntiātiō ōnis, f denuntio, an indication, announcement, declaration, proclamation, threat : denuntiationi parere: calamitatum: belli: testimoni, a summons to testify : periculi, a menace , Cs.: terroris, L.: senatū…

denuntio.definition: dē-nūntiō āvī, ātus, āre, to announce, declare, denounce, menace, threaten, intimate, order, command: inimicitias mihi: populo R. servitutem: ab amico timor denuntiari solet?: sese procuratorem esse: eos cavendos esse…

denuo.definition: dēnuō adv. de + novo, once more, a second time, anew, afresh, again : Etruria rebellans, L.: Sicilia censa denuo est: recita denuo: iube mi denuo Respondeat, T.— In turn, again (colloq.): metuo ne denuo Miser excludar…

deonero.definition: de-onerō āvī, ātus, āre, to unload, disburden: ex illius invidiā aliquid et in te traicere.

deorsum.definition: deorsum or deorsus adv. de+vorsum, vorsus.—Of motion, downwards, down : pondere ferri.—With sursum, up and down : Ne sursum deorsum cursites, T.: naturis sursum deorsum commeantibus.— Of position, down, below : Clivos…

depasco.definition: dē-pāscō pāvī, pāstus, ere, to feed down, feed off, give for food: saltūs, O.: luxuriem segetum, V.—To feed upon, graze, consume: agros: (tauri) summa Lycaei, V.: saepes Hyblaeis apibus florem depasta salicti, V.—Poet…

depecto.definition: dē-pectō —, pexus, ere, to comb off, comb down, comb: crinīs buxo, O.: depexus crinibus, O.: vellera foliis, V.—To comb down, flog, curry (colloq.), T.

depeculator.definition: dēpecūlātor ōris, m depeculor, a plunderer, embezzler : aerari: suus (i. e. eorum).

depeculor.definition: dēpecūlor ātus, ārī cf. peculium, to despoil, plunder, strip : delubra: Apollonium argento.— To embezzle, acquire by fraud : laudem familiae.

depello.definition: dē-pellō pulī, pulsus, ere, to drive out, drive away, remove, expel, put out, put off, turn aside: venientem in forum virum vi: de Falerno Anseres: eum de provinciā, N.: alqm urbe, to banish, Ta.: ab aris et focis fer…

dependeo.definition: dē-pendeō —, —, ēre, to hang from, hang on, hang down: ex umeris nodo dependet amictus, V.: galea ramis, V.: serta tectis, O.: laqueo, L.: Licia dependent, O.—Fig., to be dependent on, wait for: Dependet fides a venie…

dependo.definition: dē-pendō dī, —, ere, to pay: dependendum tibi est, quod mihi spopondisti.—Fig., to pay, render: rei p. poenas.

deperdo.definition: dē-perdō didī, ditus, ere, to destroy, ruin: sutor inopiā deperditus, i. e. impoverished, Ph.: deperditus alquā, desperately in love with, Pr.: in alquā, Ct.: fletu, exhausted, Ct.—To lose: bona, honestatem: tantum ei…

depereo.definition: dē-pereō iī, itūrus, īre, to go to ruin, perish, die, be lost, be undone: tempestate deperierant naves, Cs.: exercitū s magna pars, Cs.: qui deperiit minor uno mense, H.: gens hominum vitio deperitura fuit, O.—To be d…

depingo.definition: dē-pīngō pinxi, pictus, ere, to depict, portray, paint, draw: pugnam, N.—Fig., to portray, represent, describe, imagine, conceive: probe horum facta, T.: vitam huiusce: minuta quaedam nimiumque depicta, too elaboratel…

deplango.definition: dē-plangō nxī, —, ere, to bewail, lament (by beating the breast, etc.): plamis Deplanxere domum, O.: deplangitur Ardea pennis, O.

deploro.definition: de-plōrō āvī, ātus, āre, to weep bitterly, moan, wail, lament, complain: lamentabili voce: de isdem rebus esse dolentius deplorandum.—With acc, to bewail, lament, deplore: ad saxa haec: damnationem illam: domum incens…

depluo.definition: dē-pluō uī, —, ere, to rain down: Multus ut in terras deplueret lapis, Tb.

depono.definition: dē-pōnō posuī (-posīvī, Ct.), positus, ere, to lay away, put aside, set down, lay, place, set, deposit: lecticā paulisper depositā: corpora sub ramis arboris, V.: mentum in gremiis mimarum: onera iumentis, Cs.: deposi…

depopulatio.definition: dēpopulātiō ōnis, f depopulor, a laying waste, marauding, pillaging : agrorum: aedium: ad depopulationem profecti, L.: iter Antoniorum quid habuit nisi depopulationes?

depopulator.definition: dēpopulātor ōris, m depopulor, a marauder, pillager : fori.

depopulor.definition: dē-populor ātus, ārī, dep., to lay waste, ravage, plunder, pillage: Ambiorigis finīs, Cs.: agros, L.: extrema agri Romani, L.: domos, fana: omne mortalium genus (of pestilence), Ta.— P. pass.: depopulatis agris, laid …

deporto.definition: dē-portō āvī, ātus, āre, to carry down, carry off, take away: frumentum in castra, Cs.: ex Siciliā litteras in Verrem: ossa eius ad matrem, N.: partem exercitūs eo, Cs.: omnem exercitum ex Hispaniā, evacuate, L.—To tr…

deposco.definition: dē-pōscō popōscī, —, ere, to demand, require, request earnestly, call for: unum ad id bellum imperatorem deposci: imperatorem Caesarem: sibi navīs, Cs.: pericula, Ta.: sicut semper depoposcimus, Cs.: omnibus pollicita…

depravatio.definition: dēprāvātiō ōnis, f depravo, a distortion : quaedam (membrorum): oris.—Fig., a perversion, corruption, vitiation : animi: consuetudinum: nostra, perversity .

depravo.definition: dēprāvō —, ātus, āre de + pravus, to distort, disfigure : quaedam contra naturam depravata. — Fig., to pervert, seduce, corrupt, deprave, spoil : nil est Quin male narrando possit depravarier, T.: ut ea quae conrigere…

deprecabundus.definition: dēprecābundus adj. deprecor, earnestly entreating , Ta.

deprecatio.definition: dēprecātiō ōnis, f deprecor, an averting by prayer, appeal, intercession, plea, apology : periculi: quae deprecatio est ei reliqua, qui, etc.: aequitatis, on the ground of : pro illis, Cu.: deprecatione deorum commove…

deprecator.definition: dēprecātor ōris, m deprecor, an averter, intercessor : miseriarum: pro illius periculo.— An advocate, mediator : sui: apud consulem deprecator vobis adero, L.: salutis meae: ut eo deprecatore a Sequanis impetrarent, C…

deprecor.definition: dē-precor ātus, ārī, dep., to avert by prayer, deprecate, plead against, beg to escape, seek to avoid: ullam ab sese calamitatem: a me patriae querimoniam: nullum genus supplici: mortem, Cs.: inimici imperium, S.: sui…

deprehendo.definition: dē-prehendō or dēprēndō (-praendō ) dī, sus, ere, to take away, seize upon, catch, snatch : deprehensus ex itinere Magius, Cs.: comitatūs in ponte, S.: litterae deprehensae, intercepted, L.: navīs, to seize, Cs.: Argo…

deprehensio.definition: dēprehēnsiō ōnis, f deprehendo, a catching, discovery : manifesta veneni.

deprimo.definition: dēprimō pressī, pressus, ere de + premo, to press down, weigh down, sink down, depress : terram: ad mentum depresso supercilio: depresso aratro, V.— To sink (in water): partem navium, Cs.: carinam, O.: classis depress…

deproelior.definition: (dē-proelior,) —, ārī, dep. —P. praes., warring violently: ventos aequore Deproeliantīs, H.

depromo.definition: dē-prōmō prōmpsī, prōmptus, ere, to draw out, draw forth, bring out, fetch: pecuniam ex aerario: tela pharetris, V.: venenum sinu, Ta.— Fig., to draw, derive, obtain: e quibus locis argumenta: alqd vel a peritis vel d…

depropero.definition: dē-properō —, —, āre, to hasten, prepare hastily: coronas, H.

depudet.definition: dēpudet uit, ēre, impers, to cease to shame: depuduit, shame has departed, O.

depugis.definition: dēpūgis (depȳgis) is, adj. puga, without buttocks, thin buttocked , H.

depugno.definition: dē-pūgnō āvī, ātus, āre, to fight decisively, fight out, join battle, combat: signis conlatis, L.: acie instructā, Cs.: cum civibus: ad depugnandum, N.: ante depugnabitur: depugnatum cum Gallis est, L.—Fig., to conten…

depulsio.definition: dēpulsiō ōnis, f de+1 PAL-, a driving off, driving away, repelling, warding off : mali: servitutis.— A defence, answer (to a charge), C.— A lowering, sinking : luminum.

depulsor.definition: dēpulsor ōris, m de+1 PAL-, a destroyer : dominatū s.

deputo.definition: dē-putō āvī, ātus, āre, to cut off, prune: umbras (i. e. ramos), O.—To reckon, estimate, esteem, consider: meam esse operam parvi preti, T.: malo se dignum deputat.

derelictio.definition: dērelictiō ōnis, f derelinquo, an abandoning, disregard, neglect : communis utilitatis.

derelinquo.definition: dē-relinquō līquī, lictus, ere, to forsake wholly, abandon, desert: Gracchum a Tuberone derelictum videbamus: arationes: ab omni fortunā derelicti: filium privatum dereliquerat, S.: oppida pro derelicto habere, abando…

derepo.definition: dē-rēpō rēpsī, —, ere, to crawl down, sneak down: ad cubile suis, Ph.

derideo.definition: dē-rīdeō sī, sus, ēre, to laugh at, laugh to scorn, scoff at, deride, mock: omnīs istos: te, H.: derisum esse credo hominem: alqd, H.: derisus semel, hooted off: derideat Aethiopem albus, In.: merito, T.: deridet, cum…

deridiculus.definition: dē-rīdīculus adj., very laughable, ridiculous: deridiculum esse se reddere, etc., L. dub.—As subst n., an object of ridicule, laughing stock, mockery: deridiculo esse, Ta.: per deridiculum auditur, Ta.: corporis, ludi…

derigesco.definition: (dē-rigēscō) dēriguī, or dīriguī , —, ere, inch, to become stiff, grow rigid, fix, curdle (only perf. system): formidine sanguis deriguit, V.: deriguere oculi, were fixed, V.: hirsutae comae, O.

deripio.definition: dēripiō ripuī, reptus, ere de + rapio, to tear off, tear away, snatch away, remove violently, pull down : cothurnos, V.: de manu Cereris Victoriam: vestem a pectore, O.: velamina ex umeris, O.: ei vitae ornamenta deri…

derisor.definition: dērīsor ōris, m derideo, a mocker, scoffer : semper eris, H.: populi, Iu.: imi lecti, H.

derivatio.definition: dērīvātiō ōnis, f derivo, a leading off, turning away : (lacūs). L.—Plur: fluminum.

derivo.definition: dērīvō āvī, ātus, āre de + rivus, to lead off, turn away : aqua ex flumine derivata, Cs.—Fig., to draw, derive, bring : nihil in suam domum inde: Hoc fonte derivata clades, H.— To divert, turn aside, transfer : in me …

derogatio.definition: dērogātiō ōnis, f derogo, a partial abrogation, limitation (of a law).

derogo.definition: dē-rogō āvī, ātus, āre.—In legislation, to repeal in part, restrict, modify: neque derogari ex hac (lege) aliquid licet: de lege aliquid derogare. —In gen., to take away, detract, diminish, impair, withhold: de magnif…

derosus.definition: dē-rōsus P., gnawed away, nibbled: clipei a muribus.

deruo.definition: dē-ruō ruī, —, ere, to take away, detract: cumulum de laudibus alicuius.

deruptus.definition: dē-ruptus adj. with comp, broken, precipitous, steep: angustiae, L.: in deruptiorem tumulum, L. — Plur n. as subst, precipices, L.

desaevio.definition: dē-saeviō iī, —, īre, to rave furiously, rage: in aequore, V.: pelago hiems, V.: tragicā in arte, H.

descendo.definition: dē-scendō dī, sus, ere, to climb down, come down, descend, fall, sink: ex equo, to alight: monte, S.: de palatio: caelo, H.: e caelo, Iu.: vertice montis ab alto, V.: ab Alpibus, L.: arce Monoeci, V.: per clivum, O.: …

descensio.definition: dēscēnsiō ōnis, f descendo, a descending : Tiberina, the sail down the Tiber .

descisco.definition: dē-scīscō īvī, ītus, ere, to withdraw, leave, revolt from, desert, go over: ab Afranio, Cs.: a populo: quibus invitis descitum ad Samnites erat, L.: aperte, L.— In gen., to depart, deviate, withdraw, fall off, be unfa…

describo.definition: dē-scrībō īpsī, īptus, ere (often confounded with discribo), to copy off, transcribe, write out, write down: a te librum (i. e. a tuo exemplo): descriptam legem adferunt, the draf<*> in foliis carmina, V.: in cortice …

descriptio.definition: dēscrīptiō ōnis (often confounded with discriptio), f describo, a marking out, delineation, copy, transcript, draft : caeli, circuit : tabularum: alqd descriptionibus explicare.—Fig., a representation, delineation, de…

deseco.definition: dē-secō cuī, ctus, āre, to cut off, cut away: aurīs, Cs.: cervice desectā, L.: particulam undique, H.: hordeum, Cs.: desecta cum stramento seges, L.: Desectum gramen, O.—Fig., to prune off, reject: illud (prooemium).

desero.definition: dē-serō ruī, rtus, ere, to leave, forsake, abandon, desert, give up: exercitum, Cs.: castra, L.: castellis desertis, Cs.: fratrem, V.: thalamos pactos, V.: Mensa deserit toros, is removed from, O.: Raro scelestum Dese…

desertor.definition: dēsertor ōris, m desero, one who forsakes, a deserter : amicorum: communis utilitatis aut salutis.—In war, a runaway, deserter , Cs., L., Ta.— Poet.: Amoris, O.: Asiae, V.

deservio.definition: dē-serviō —, —, īre, to serve zealously, be devoted, be subject, be of service: cuivis deserviant: vobis operā deservire: si officia, si operae, si vigiliae deserviunt amicis: divinis rebus.

desideo.definition: dēsideō sēdī, —, ēre de + sedeo, to sit long, sit idle, remain inactive : totum diem, T.: aquila ramis, Ph.

desiderabilis.definition: dēsīderābilis e, adj. desidero, wanted, desirable : nihil desiderabile concupiscunt: suis vitiis desiderabilem efficere avum, i. e. missed , L.: princeps, Ta.

desideratio.definition: dēsīderātiō ōnis, f desidero, a desiring, longing, missing : (voluptatum) dub

desiderium.definition: dēsīderium ī, n cf. desidero, a longing, ardent desire, wish, want, grief, regret : Athenarum, T.: urbis, homesickness : coniunctissimi viri: tam cari capitis, H.: pectora diu tenet desiderium, Enn. ap. C.: Ita magno …

desidero.definition: dēsīderō āvī, ātus, āre cf. considero, to long for, ask, demand, call for, wish for, desire, require, expect : me, T.: tribuni imperium, Cs.: ea (beneficia), S.: quod satis est, H.: ullam rem ad se inportari, Cs.: alq…

desidia.definition: dēsidia ae, f deses, a sitting idle, idleness, inactivity, sloth : ab industriā ad desidiam avocari: pro labore desidia, S.: latrocinia desidiae minuendae causā fieri, Cs.: improba Siren, H.: invisa primo desidia post…

desidiosus.definition: dēsidiōsus adj. with sup. desidia, slothful, indolent, lazy, idle : Qui nolet fieri desidiosus, amet, O.— Causing idleness, making lazy : inlecebrae cupiditatum: desidiosissimum otium.

desido.definition: dē-sīdō sīdī, —, ere.—Of places, to sink, settle down, fall: ut multis locis terrae desiderint: ad Manīs imos, V.—Fig., to deteriorate: desidentes mores, L.

designatio.definition: dēsīgnātiō ōnis, f designo, a marking out, specification (cf. dissignatio): personarum et temporum.— A designation to office : annua, of consuls , Ta.

designo.definition: dē-sīgnō āvī, ātus, āre, to mark out, point out, trace, designate, define (often confounded with dissigno): urbem aratro, V.: moenia fossā, V.: templo Iovis finīs, L.: circo designatus locus est, L.: Europen, depicts …

desino.definition: dē-sinō siī (rare; dēstitī is used instead), situs, ere, to leave off, give over, cease, desist, forbear: lacessere, T.: de compositione loqui, Cs.: furere: iudicia severa Romae fieri desierunt: ut auctor Desinat inqu…

desipio.definition: dēsipiō —, —, ere de + sapio, to be void of understanding, be silly, act foolishly : licet me desipere dicatis: si non desipit augur, H.: Dulce est desipere in loco, to trifle , H.

desisto.definition: dē-sistō stitī, stitus, ere, to leave off, cease, give over, desist from: de quā (petitione) ne aliquid iurares destitisti: de petitione, L.: a defensione, Cs.: ab oppugnatione, S.: litibus, T.: hoc conatu, Cs.: susce…

desolo.definition: dē-sōlō āvī, ātus, āre, to leave alone, forsake, abandon, desert: agros, V.: desolatae terrae, O.: desolatus servilibus ministeriis, deprived of, Ta.

despecto.definition: dēspectō —, —, āre, intens. despicio, to look down upon : terras, V., O.: Palantīs homines procul, O.— To overlook, command : quos despectant moenia, V.— To despise : liberos, Ta.

desperatio.definition: dēspērātiō ōnis, f despero, hopelessness, despair : summa, Cs.: ad desperationem adducti, N.: a desperatione iram accendit, L.: desperationes eorum, qui, etc.: vitae: nimis celer rerum, L.: magna pacis, Cs.

despero.definition: dē-spērō āvī, ātus, āre, to be hopeless, have no hope, despair of, give up: de se: de pugnā , Cs.: de toto ordine: de summā rerum, L.: honores: rem p.: vitam: voluntariam deditionem, L.: sive restituimur, sive despera…

despicatio.definition: dēspicātiō ōnis, f 1 despicatus, contempt .— Only plur, sentiments of contempt .

despicientia.definition: dēspicientia ae, f despiciens, a despising, contempt : rerum humanarum: animi.

despicio.definition: dēspiciō ēxī, ectus, ere de + specio, to look down upon : de vertice montis in vallīs, O.: colles, quā despici poterat, in the range of view , Cs.— With acc , (some read dispicio in these passages): gentīs et urbīs: a…

despolio.definition: de-spoliō āvī, ātus, āre, to rob, plunder, despoil: se armis, Cs.: ut cum Siculis despoliaretur: despoliari triumpho, L.

despondeo.definition: dē-spondeō spondī, spōnsus, ēre, to promise to give, promise, pledge: librum alicui: Romanis imperium Orientis, L.— To promise in marriage, betroth, engage: ei filiam suam: virgo desponsa uni ex Curiatiis, L.: tibi Ia…

despumo.definition: dē-spūmō —, —, āre, to skim off, skim: foliis undam aëni, V.

despuo.definition: dē-spuō —, —, ere, to spit out, spit upon: ubi despui religio est, L.: in molles sibi sinūs, Tb.— To reject, abhor: preces, Ct.

destillo.definition: dē-stīllō or dī-stīllō —, —, āre, to drip, trickle down: destillat ab inguine virus, V.: Illius puro destillent tempora Nardo, Tb.

destinatio.definition: dēstinātiō ōnis, f destino, an assignment : partium, L.— A resolve, determination : haud dubia, Ta.: destinationis certus, resolute , Ta.

destino.definition: dēstinō āvī, ātus, āre STA-, to make fast, make firm, bind, fix, stay : antemnas ad malos, Cs.: rates ancoris, Cs.—Fig., to fix in mind, determine, resolve, design, assign, devote, appoint, appropriate : eum ducem, fi…

destituo.definition: dēstituō uī, ūtus, ere de + statuo, to set down, set forth, put away, bring forward, leave alone : alios in convivio (in mockery): ante tribunal regis destitutus, L.: ante pedes destitutum causam dicere, L.— To leave,…

destitutio.definition: dēstitūtiō ōnis, f destituo, an abandonment, desertion, disappointment : destitutione irati.

destrictus.definition: dēstrictus adj. P. of destringo, severe, rigid . — Only comp: destrictior accusator, Ta.

destringo.definition: dē-stringo inxī, ictus, ere, to strip off: tunica ab umeris destricta est, Ph.—To unsheathe, draw: gladios in rem p.: gladiis destrictis impetum facere, Cs.: ensem, H.: in se destrictis securis, brandished, L.—To touc…

destruo.definition: dē-struō ūxī, ūctus, ere, to tear down, raze, demolish: navem: moenia, V.—Fig., to destroy, ruin, weaken: id (ius), L.: senem, O.: hostem, Ta.

desudo.definition: dē-sūdō —, —, āre, to sweat, make great exertion: in his (sc. exercitationibus ingeni).

desuetudo.definition: dēsuētūdō nis, f desuetus, disuse, want of practice : armorum, L.: desuetudine tardi, O.

desultor.definition: dēsultor ōris, m de + 2 SAL-, a vaulter, circus-rider : desultorum in modum, L.—Fig.: amoris, i. e. inconstant , O.

desultorius.definition: dēsultōrius adj. desultor, of a vaulter : quasi desultorius, like a circus-rider's horse .

desum.definition: dē-sum fuī, esse (in poetry dee- is one syll.; perf. dēfuērunt, trisyl., O.; fut. inf. dēfutūrum esse or dēfore), to be away, be absent, fail, be wanting, be missing: quasi desit locus, T.: Non ratio, verum argentum d…

desumo.definition: dē-sūmō ūmpsī, —, ere, to take, choose, select: tibi hostīs, L.: sibi vacuas Athenas, H.—To assume, undertake: sibi consules adservandos, L.

desuper.definition: dē-super adv. —Of motion, from above, from overhead: (alqm) volnerare, Cs.: nemus imminet, V.—Of rest, above (poet.): imposuere togas, O.

desurgo.definition: dē-surgō —, —, ere, to rise: cenā, H.

detego.definition: dē-tegō ēxī, ēctus, ere, to uncover, expose, lay bare, unroof: aedem, L.: Caci detecta regia, V.: iuga montium detexerat nebula, L.: caput puer detectus, with bare head, V.: ossa, O.: detecta corpora: arcana profanā m…

detendo.definition: dē-tendō —, sus, ere, to unstretch: tabernaculis detensis, struck, Cs.: tabernacula, L.

detergeo.definition: dē-tergeō (plur. once detergunt, L.), sī, sus, ere, to wipe off, wipe away: lacrimas pollice, O.: nubila caelo, i. e. to clear, H.—To wipe, cleanse: volnera mappā , Iu.: cloacas, L.—To strip off, break off: remos, Cs.…

deterior.definition: dēterior ius, adj. comp. with sup. dēterrimus de, lower, worse, poorer, meaner : tempus, less favorable : status: vectigalia sibi deteriora facere, Cs.: muraena carne, H.: aetas, V.: quo (peditatu) erat deteriore, i. …

determinatio.definition: dēterminātiō ōnis, f determino, a boundary, conclusion : mundi: orationis.

determino.definition: dē-terminō āvī, ātus, āre, to enclose, bound, limit, prescribe: regiones ab oriente ad occasum, L.—To fix, settle, determine: spiritu, non arte, ends (his sentences): Omnia determinat annus, C. poët.

detero.definition: dē-terō trīvī, trītus, ere, to rub away, wear away: detritae aequore conchae, O.: pedes (via), Tb.: a catenā collum detritum, Ph.—Fig., to lessen, weaken, impair: laudes Caesaris culpā ingeni, H.: Exiguis (rebus) aliq…

deterreo.definition: dē-terreō uī, itus, ēre, to frighten off, deter, discourage, prevent, hinder: reliquos magnitudine poenae, Cs.: testīs verbis: pavidam ense, O.: deterritis tribunis, L.: in deterrendā liberalitate. adulescentīs a dice…

detestabilis.definition: dētestābilis e, adj. with comp. detestor, execrable, abominable, detestable : omen: nihil esse tam detestabile quam voluptatem: exemplum, L.: detestabilior immanitas.

detestatio.definition: dētestātiō ōnis, f detestor, the invocation of a curse : eā detestatione obstricti, L.: dira, H. — An averting by sacrifice, deprecation : scelerum.

detexo.definition: dē-texō —, xtus, ere, to weave, plait: aliquid Viminibus, V.: fiscellam vimine, Tb.—Fig.: detexta prope retexantur, finished.

detineo.definition: dētineō tinuī, tentus, ēre de + teneo, to hold off, keep back, detain, check : a quo incepto me ambitio detinuerat, S.: me detinuit morbus, T.: civium numerum tam bonis rebus: contionibus detinenda plebs, L.: me his o…

detondeo.definition: dē-tondeō —, tōnsus, ēre, to shear off, cut off, clip, shear: crinīs, O.: detonsae frigore frondes, i. e. stripped off, O.

detono.definition: dē-tonō uī, —, āre, to thunder down, thunder: (Iuppiter) ubi detonuit, O.—To have done thundering: nubem belli, dum detonet omnis, Sustinet, exhaust its rage, V.

detorqueo.definition: dē-torqueō sī, tus, ēre, to bend aside, turn off, turn away, turn, direct: ponticulum: Ora dextrā equorum, V.: lumen ab illā, O.: volnus, averted, V.: alqd in dextram partem: ad regem cursūs, V.: cervicem ad oscula, H…

detractio.definition: dētrāctiō ōnis, f detraho, a taking away, wresting, withdrawal, removal : (Praxitelia capita) efficiuntur detractione, cutting away : alieni: cibi, a purging .

detractor.definition: dētrāctor ōris, m de + TRAG-, a disparager : sui, Ta.

detraho.definition: dē-trahō trāxī, trāctus, ere, to draw off, take down, pull down, take away, remove, withdraw, drag, bring: soccos detrahunt (servi), T.: detractis insignibus imperatoris, Cs.: vestem: pellem, H.: alquem in iudicium: d…

detrectatio.definition: dētrectātiō (dētrāct-) ōnis, f detrecto, a declining, refusing : militiae, L.: sine detrectatione, L.

detrimentosus.definition: dētrīmentōsus adj. detrimentum, hurtful, detrimental : discedere detrimentosum esse, Cs.

detrimentum.definition: dētrīmentum ī, n de + 1 TER-, that which is worn away : ergastuli detrimenta (of men), wrecks of the work-house , Cu.— Wear and tear, loss, damage, detriment : exercitūs, Cs.: militum, Cs.: existimationis, N.: de te f…

detrudo.definition: dē-trūdō sī, sus, ere, to thrust away, thrust down, push down, push off, strip off: in pistrinum: in solidam acumina (pedum) erram, O.: caput sub Tartara telo, V.: sub inania Tartara, O.: navīs scopulo, V.: scutis teg…

detrunco.definition: dē-truncō āvī, ātus, āre, to lop, cut off: arbores, L.: caput, O.—To mutilate, maim, behead: gladio detruncata corpora, L.

deturbo.definition: dē-turbō āvī, ātus, āre, to thrust down, beat down, expel, overthrow, tear down, hurl, strike down: ex turribus propugnantīs, Cs.: ex praesidiis Macedonas, L.: lapidibus coniectis deturbati, dislodged, Cs.: nitentīs p…

deuro.definition: de-ūrō ūssī, ūstus, ere, to burn up, consume, destroy: deusti plutei turrium, Cs.: vicum, L.—Of frost: hiems arbores deusserat, L.

deus.definition: deus ī (nom plur. dī, diī, rarely deī ; gen. deōrum or deūm, poet. also divōm or divū m; dat. dīs, diīs, and later deīs), m DIV-, a god, deity : deorum inmortalium numen: consilio deorum, Cs.— In ejaculations: di! T.:…

deutor.definition: de-ūtor —, ūtī, dep., to maltreat: victo, N.

devasto.definition: dē-vāstō —, ātus, āre, to lay waste, devastate: finīs, L.: Marsos, L.: agmina ferro devastata, O.

deveho.definition: de-vehō vexī, vectus, ere, to carry down, carry off, convey, take away: (carinas) carris iunctis milia passuum a castris XXII, Cs.: legionem equis, Cs.: maximos commeatūs Tiberis devexit, L.: devecta cremato sarmenta,…

develo.definition: dē-vēlō —, —, āre, to unveil, uncover: Ora sororis, O.

deveneror.definition: dē-veneror ātus, ārī, dep., to reverence, worship: deos prece, O.—To avert by prayer: somnia, Tb.

devenio.definition: dē-veniō vēnī, ventūrus, īre, to come, arrive, reach: alquam in partem, Cs.: ad eam necessario: in victoris manūs: in eum locum, L.: in Scythiam, O.: quo, H.—With acc: devenere locos ubi, etc., V.: speluncam eandem, V…

deverbero.definition: dē-verberō āvī, —, āre, to thrash, cudgel soundly: homines usque ad necem, T.

deversor.definition: dē-versor (-vorsor) ātus, ārī, dep., to tarry, put up, lodge as a guest: Athenis apud eum: apud Ninnios, L.: hac in domo tam diu: domi suae: parum laute.

deversoriolum.definition: dēversōriolum ī, n dim. deversorium, a small lodging-place .

deversorium.definition: dēversōrium (dēvors-, dīvers-) ī, n deversor, an inn, lodging-house : commorandi: hospitale, L.: flagitiorum omnium: nota, H.

deverticulum.definition: dēverticulum (dīvert-, dēvort-) ī, n deverto, a by-road, by-path, side-way : quae deverticula quaesivisti?: Ubi ad ipsum veni devorticulum, T.— An inn, lodging-house, tavern : omnia loca deverticuli protraherentur, L.…

deverto.definition: dē-vertō or dēvortō tī, —, ere, to turn away, turn aside, turn in, put up, betake oneself, go to lodge: viā devertit, loses the way, L.: ad coponem: eius domum: in villam Pompei.—Fig., to digress: redeamus illuc, unde…

devexus.definition: dēvexus adj. deveho, inclining, sloping, shelving, steep : lucus a Palati radice in novam viam: mundus in Austros, V.: amnis, V.: haec declivia et devexa, Cs.: arva, O.: Orion, i. e. towards his setting , H.: raeda, o…

devincio.definition: dē-vinciō nxī, nctus, ere, to bind fast, tie up, fetter, clamp: aliquem fasciis: operculis plumbo devinctis, L.—Fig., to bind fast, unite closely, oblige, lay under obligation: (Italiam) omnibus vinclis devinctam tene…

devinco.definition: dē-vincō vīcī, vīctus, ere, to conquer completely, overcome, subdue: Galliam, Cs.: Capuam: Poenos classe: devicti reges, H.: devicta Asia, V.: devicto (mihi) restabat, O.: devicta bella, victoriously concluded, V.—Fig…

devitatio.definition: dēvītātiō ōnis, f devito, an avoiding : legionum.

devito.definition: dē-vītō āvī, ātus, āre, to avoid, shun: procellam temporis: Quae (mala), T.: repulsam, H.

devius.definition: dēvius adj. de + via, off the road, out of the way, devious : iter, a by-way : oppidum: calles, L.: rura, O.— Retired, sequestered : Anagnini: gens, L.: mihi devio libet, etc., wandering in byways , H.: avis, i. e. th…

devoco.definition: dē-vocō āvī, ātus, āre, to call off, call away, recall: eum de provinciā: ab tumulo suos, L.: ex praesidiis, L.: refixa sidera caelo, H.: Iovem ad auxilium, L.—Fig., to call off, allure, bring down: philosophiam e cae…

devolo.definition: dē-volō —, ātūrus, āre, to fly down: Iris per caelum, V.: sibi de caelo devolatura in sinum victoria, L.—To fly away: turdus devolet illuc, ubi, etc., H.—To hasten down, hasten away, fly: praecipites pavore in forum, …

devolvo.definition: dē-volvō volvī, volūtus, ere, to roll down: saxa in musculum, Cs.: Auratas trabes, V.: tonitrua (i. e. balls to make scenic thunder), Ph.: corpora in humum, O.: magnos corpore montīs, O.: fusis mollia pensa, i. e. to …

devoro.definition: dē-vorō āvī, ātus, āre, to swallow, gulp down, devour, consume: id quod devoratur: Pro epulis auras, O.—To swallow up, ingulf, absorb: devorer telluris hiatu, O.: vel me Charybdis devoret, O.— To seize greedily, swall…

devortium.definition: dēvortium ī deverto, a by-way : devortia itinerum, Ta. (al. div-).

devotio.definition: dēvōtiō ōnis, f devoveo, a self-sacrifice, offering : eius devotionis convictus: vitae: capitis.— A cursing, execration, outlawry : eius devotionis memoria, N.: in quibus (pilis) scripta, N.— A formula of execration ,…

devoveo.definition: dē-voveō vōvī, vōtus, ēre, to vow, devote, offer, sacrifice: Marti ea, quae bello ceperint, Cs.: Dianae alqd pulcherrimum: gnatam pro mutā agnā, H.: se ipsos dis pro re p.: se pro patriā, L.: se aris, V.: auspicio se:…

dextella.definition: dextella ae, f dim. dextra, a little right hand : Q. filius illius est dextella.

dexter.definition: dexter tera, terum, and tra, trum, adj. with comp. dexterior and sup. dextimus, to the right, on the right side, right (opp. laevus, sinister): manus: umeri, Cs.: latus, H.: hostium, Cs.: cornum, T.: cornu, Cs.: acies…

dexteritas.definition: dexteritās ātis, f dexter, dexterity, aptness : ad omnia ingeni dexteritas, L.

dextrorsum.definition: dextrōrsum or dextrōrsus adv. dexter + vorsus, towards the right side, to the right : dextrorsum abire, H.: dextrorsus pergere, L.

diadema.definition: diadēma ātis, n , dia/dhma, a royal headdress, diadem: conlegae diadema imponere: tutum, H.

diaeta.definition: diaeta ae, f , di/aita, a regular mode of living, diet: diaetā curari.

dialectice.definition: dialecticē adv. dialecticus, logically, dialectically : disputare: dicta multa.

dialecticus.definition: dialecticus adj. , dialektiko/s, belonging to disputation, dialectic: captiones.—As subst m., a dialectician, logician.

dialogus.definition: dialogus ī, m , dia/logos, a discussion, treatise in conversational form, dialogue.

diarium.definition: (diārium ī), n dies, a daily ration (only plur.): diariis militum celeritatem incitat: cum servis diaria rodere, H.

dibaphus.definition: dibaphus ī, f , di/bafos (prop. double dyed), a purple robe, magistrate's state-robe.

dica.definition: dica ae, f , di/kh, a lawsuit, judicial process, action: omnibus dicis diem distulit, adjourned all actions.—In the phrases: dicam scribere, to bring an action: tibi scribam dicam, against thee, T.: iniuriarum mihi sc…

dicacitas.definition: dicācitās ātis, f dicax, biting wit, raillery .

dicatio.definition: dicātiō ōnis, f 1 dico, a formal declaration (in changing one's citizenship).

dicax.definition: dicāx ācis, adj. with comp. DIC-, talking sharply, satirical, sarcastic, acute, witty : Demosthenes: Satyri, wanton , H.: dicacior naturā , L.

dichoreus.definition: dichorēus ī, m , dixo/reios, a double trochee.

dicio.definition: (diciō) ōnis, f DIC-, dominion, sovereignty, authority, sway, control, rule (only sing; no nom.): oram Romanae dicionis fecit, brought under , L.: regna virūm dicioni permissa: civitates in dicionem populi R. redactas…

dictamnus.definition: dictamnus ī, f , =di/ktamnos, dittany (an herb), C., V.

dictator.definition: dictātor ōris, m dicto.—In Rome, a dictator, chief magistrate with unlimited power (in great emergencies, superseding ordinary magistracies): lex de dictatore lata, Cs.: nomen dictatoris sustulisti: creandi dictatoris…

dictatorius.definition: dictātōrius adj. dictator, of a dictator, dictatorial : stilus: maiestas, L.: iuvenis, i. e. the son of the dictator , L.

dictio.definition: dictiō ōnis, f DIC-, a saying, speaking, uttering, delivery : testimoni, i. e. the right of giving testimony , T.: causae, a pleading .—Esp., in the phrase, iuris dictio, the administration of justice : ut iuris dicti…

dictito.definition: dictitō āvī, ātus, āre, intens. dicto, to say often, declare, maintain, assert, insist : non es Quem semper te esse dictitasti? T.: qui ita dictitat, iis esse metuendum, etc.: si te populus sanum dictitet, H.— To plea…

dicto.definition: dīctō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. 2 dico, to dictate, suggest, remind : tu idem, qui illis orationem dictavisses, put in their mouths : Mercemur servum qui dictet nomina (i. e. nomenclatorem), H.: Tironi (opp. ipse scribere…

diduco.definition: dī-dūcō dūxī, ductus, ere, to draw apart, part, split, separate, sever, sunder, divide, undo, relax: digitos: risu rictum Auditoris, H.: nodos manu, O.: arva et urbīs, V.: fores, Ta.: scopulos (Hannibal), Iu.: vestem,…

diductio.definition: dīductiō ōnis, f diduco, a divergence, opposite conclusion : rationis.

diecula.definition: diēcula ae, f dim. dies, a little while, respite , T., C.

dies.definition: diēs gen. diēī or diē (rarely diei, disyl., T., or diī, V.), m sometimes in sing f. DIV-, a day, civil day : Quae tot res in unum conclusit diem, T.: eo die, Cs.: in posterum diem, Cs.: paucos dies ibi morati, Cs.: al…

diffamo.definition: (diffāmō) —, ātus, āre dis- + fama, to make a scandal of, divulge : adulterium diffamatum, O.: prava, Ta.— To malign : viros procacibus scriptis, Ta.

differentia.definition: differentia ae, f differo, a difference, diversity : honesti et decori: in principiis.— A species : (opp. genus).

differo.definition: differō distulī, dīlātus, ferre dis- + fero, to carry apart, spread abroad, scatter, disperse, separate : venti magnitudine ignem, Cs.: Nubila, V.: rudentis (Eurus), H.: in versum ulmos, i. e. planted , V.: Mettum in …

differtus.definition: differtus adj. dis- + farcio, stuffed, crammed, crowded, swarming : provincia differta exactoribus, Cs.: corpus odoribus, Ta.: differtum forum populumque (i. e. forum differtum populo), H.

difficilis.definition: difficilis e, adj. with comp. and sup. dis- + facilis, hard, difficult, troublesome, impracticable, laborious, perilous : res, T.: facilia ex difficillimis redigere, Cs.: opus: locus: in locos difficilī s abire, S.: v…

difficultas.definition: difficultās ātis (gen plur. -tātium, L.), f difficilis, difficulty, trouble, distress, poverty, want, embarrassment : discendi: navigandi, Cs.: faciundi pontis, Cs.: loci, S.: vecturae: summa navium: rei frumentariae,…

difficulter.definition: difficulter adv. difficilis, with difficulty, hardly : fiebat, Cs.: haud difficulter persuasum Latinis, L.; see difficiliter.

diffidenter.definition: diffīdenter diffidens, distrustfully, diffidently : diffidenter attingere aliquid: agere, L.

diffidentia.definition: diffīdentia ae, f diffidens, mistrust, distrust, diffidence : fidentiae contrarium est: rei, S.: non tam diffidentiā, futura quae imperavisset, quam, etc., S.

diffido.definition: diffīdo fīsus sum, ere dis- + fido, to distrust, be diffident, be distrustful, despair : iacet, diffidit: sui, S.: sibi aliquā ratione: eius fidei: suis rebus, Cs.: exercitui, S.: summae rei, Cs.: armis, V.: cur M. Va…

diffindo.definition: diffindō fidī, fissus, ere dis- + findo, to cleave asunder, split, divide . saxo diffisso: diffissā nate, H.: tempora plumbo, V.: portas muneribus, i. e. to open , H.—Fig., to detract : nihil hinc diffindere possum, c…

diffingo.definition: diffingō —, —, ere dis- + fingo, to transform, remodel, make anew : ferrum incude, H. — Fig.: alqd, alter , H.

diffiteor.definition: diffiteor —, ērī dis + fateor, to disavow, deny : opus, O.

diffluo.definition: diffluō fluxī, —, ere dis- + fluo, to flow in different directions, flow away : in plurīs partīs (Rhenus), branches , Cs.; cf. nos quasi extra ripas diffluentīs coercere.— To be dissolved : iecur, L.: sudore, Ph.— To …

diffugio.definition: diffugiō fūgī, —, ere dis- + fugio, to fly apart, flee in different directions, disperse, scatter : metu perterriti diffugimus: Diffugimus visu exsangues, V.: diffugiunt stellae, O.: nives, disappear , H.: sollicitudi…

diffugium.definition: diffugium ī, n dis + 2 FVG-, a dispersion. —Plur. : proximorum, Ta.

diffundo.definition: diffundō fūdī, fūsus, ere dis- + fundo, to spread by pouring, pour out, pour forth : sanguis in omne corpus diffunditur: tum freta diffundi iussit, O.: vina iterum (consule) Tauro diffusa, bottled , H.: in alqm venenu…

diffututus.definition: diffutūtus adj., exhausted by indulgence, Ct.

digamma.definition: digamma atis, n , di/gamma, the digamma: tuum, your letter F (for fenus), i. e. your interestbook.

digero.definition: dī-gerō gessī, gestus, ere, to force apart, separate, divide, distribute: In canes totidem digestus Cerberus, O.: Nilus septem in cornua, O.—Poet.: novem volucrīs in belli digerit annos, i. e. interprets to mean years…

digestio.definition: dīgestiō ōnis, f digero, an enumeration .

digitulus.definition: digitulus ī, m dim. digitus, a little finger , T.: aniculae collum digitulis oblidere.

digitus.definition: digitus ī, m DIC-, a finger : de digito anulum detraho, T.: digitos impellere, ut Scriberent: Indice monstrare digito, H.: illam digito uno attingere, to touch gently , T.: alqd extremis digitis attingere, to touch li…

digladior.definition: dī-gladior atus, ārī, dep. gladius, to fight for life and death, contend fiercely : cives inter se sicis. —Fig.: de alquā re: digladientur illi per me licet.

dignatio.definition: dīgnātiō ōnis, f dignor, honor, rank : de dignatione laborat: principum, L.: principis, Ta.

dignitas.definition: dīgnitās ātis, f dignus, worth, merit, desert, character : tantum apud me dignitas potest, Cs.: honos dignitate impetratus: consularis, a claim to the consulship : pro dignitate laudare.— Greatness, majesty, dignity, …

digno.definition: dīgnō —, —, āre dignus, to deem worthy : cunctas nomine, C. poët.: laude dignari: coniugio Veneris dignate, V.

dignus.definition: dīgnus adj. with comp. and sup. DEC-, worthy, deserving, meritorious, deserved, suitable, fitting, becoming, proper : quod te dignumst facere, T.: vir maioribus suis dignissimus: adsentatio, quae ne libero quidem dign…

digredior.definition: dīgredior gressus, ī, dep. dis- + gradior, to go apart, go asunder, separate, part, go away, depart : Hos digrediens adfabar, at parting , V.: dein digrediens, stepping aside , S.: luna tum congrediens cum sole, tum d…

digressio.definition: dīgressiō ōnis, f digredior, a parting, separating : nostra.—Fig., a digression : a propositā oratione.

dilabor.definition: dī-lābor lapsus, ī, dep., to fall asunder, go to pieces, melt away, dissolve: glacies dilapsa: nix, L.: Volcanus (i. e. ignis), H.: Fibrenus, et divisus aequaliter rapideque dilapsus, flowing apart: ungula in quinos d…

dilacero.definition: dī-lacerō āvī, ātus, āre, to tear to pieces, tear apart: dominum, O.: corpus tormentis, Ta.—Fig., to tear to pieces, waste: ad dilacerandam rem p.: opes, O.: acerbitatibus dilaceratus, Ta.

dilanio.definition: dī-laniō āvī, ātus, āre, to tear to pieces, mutilate: (cadaver) canibus dilaniandum: alqm tormentis, Ta.: membra, O.

dilapido.definition: dī-lapidō —, —, āre, to throw away, squander, consume: triginta minas, T.

dilargior.definition: dī-largior ītus, īrī, dep., to give liberally, lavish: omnia quibus voluit: foedera sociis, Ta.

dilatio.definition: dīlātiō ōnis, f dis- + TAL-, a putting off, postponement, delay : vel minime temporis: comitiorum: nulla, L.: per dilationes bellum geri, L.

dilato.definition: dīlātō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. dilatus, to spread out, dilate, broaden, stretch, enlarge, extend : manum: fundum: castra, L.: rictūs, O. — Fig., to spread, amplify, dilate, extend : orationem: haec: gloriam: litteras, t…

dilaudo.definition: dī-laudō to distinguish by praise, eulogize: libros.

diligens.definition: dīligēns entis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of diligo, industrious, careful, assiduous, attentive, diligent, accurate, scrupulous, faithful : diligentissimi aratores: homo, thrifty : servi: in re hereditariā: in osten…
